business_problem: La Trobe University needed faster access to approved research knowledge and a quicker way to turn research findings into market-ready applications, but manual knowledge discovery and limited development capacity slowed both goals.
solution_summary: La Trobe University worked with IBM on two connected generative-AI use cases built on IBM Watson Discovery, IBM watsonx Assistant and IBM watsonx.ai. In the first, researchers implemented a retrieval-augmented generation architecture over more than 100 autism papers so they could query university-approved knowledge without manually searching every document. Discovery handled source retrieval, watsonx.ai generated grounded responses and watsonx Assistant exposed the interaction layer. In the second, the same IBM watsonx portfolio was used to co-design an application that helped researchers transform their expertise into market-facing offerings much faster than traditional development approaches. The overall architecture paired governed knowledge retrieval with rapid application delivery, letting the university use one AI stack both to streamline research operations and to shorten the path from research insight to deployable solution.

solution_components.name: IBM Watson Discovery
solution_components.role: Retrieves relevant passages from the university's approved research corpus for RAG-based answers.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx Assistant
solution_components.role: Provides the conversational interface researchers use to query approved knowledge and interact with the solution.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Generates answers and supports rapid development of AI-driven applications built on university expertise.

data_flow: Approved research papers are ingested into Discovery, user questions flow through watsonx Assistant, Discovery supplies relevant passages to watsonx.ai for RAG-based answers, and the same IBM watsonx stack supports application development for market-facing use cases.
business_outcome: La Trobe shortened research access and application delivery cycles at the same time, proving that a governed RAG architecture can reduce development costs, accelerate market entry and help academic teams operationalize expertise much faster.
architecture_clues: The first use case was a RAG proof of concept over more than 100 autism papers.
The same IBM watsonx portfolio was used both for research operations and go-to-market application design.
The university chose in-house development on watsonx Assistant instead of outsourcing.
evidence_quotes: The university reduced development time from months to weeks
